rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Gravitational redshift of gamma rays over a 22.5 m tower; (5.13 +/- 0.51)e-15 vs 4.92e-15 predicted.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Predicted relativistic time gains for caesium clocks flown around the world (-40 +/- 23 ns east, 275 +/- 21 ns west).

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Observed relativistic time gains (-59 +/- 10 ns east, 273 +/- 7 ns west).

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Gravity Probe A (SAO / NASA, Vessot et al.)
rows.note: Space-borne hydrogen maser to ~10,000 km; gravitational frequency shift agrees with prediction to ~70 ppm.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Two Al+ optical clocks, 33 cm height difference; (4.1 +/- 1.6)e-17 measured vs 3.6e-17 predicted.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Gravitational redshift resolved across one millimetre within a single strontium atom cloud; one collaboration at that scale.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Prediction of the gravitational redshift and the clock-rate dependence on potential; the derivation parent for T.01's DERIVED claims.

rows.label: OPEN
rows.note: Standard survey of experimental tests of general relativity; anchors the OPEN statement that the measurements do not pick between the two descriptions.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Special relativity: the Lorentz factor and time dilation; derivation parent for the four-velocity statement.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Transverse Doppler shift of canal rays: first laboratory measurement of time dilation.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.collaboration: Botermann et al. (GSI ESR storage ring)
rows.note: Li+ ions at about a third of c: Lorentz time dilation confirmed at high precision.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Relativity in the Global Positioning System: the derivation of the ~38 us/day net satellite clock offset.

rows.label: BOUND
rows.note: GRB 221009A: Lorentz-invariance violation bounds E_QG,1 > 10 E_Pl and E_QG,2 > 6e-8 E_Pl at 95% CL.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: The foundation of general relativity: field equation whose weak-field static limit is Poisson's equation.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Final result: eta(Ti,Pt) = (-1.5 +/- 2.3 stat +/- 1.5 syst) x 1e-15.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Torsion-balance test of the equivalence principle: eta(Be,Ti) = (0.3 +/- 1.8) x 1e-13.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Lunar laser ranging test of the equivalence principle for Earth and Moon falling toward the Sun.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Antihydrogen falls down: a = (0.75 +/- 0.13 +/- 0.16) g; one collaboration, no independent replication.

rows.label: OPEN
rows.note: Survey of equivalence-principle and metric tests; anchors the OPEN statement about what fixes G and why universality holds.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Molecular-beam magnetic resonance: a two-level system driven at its Bohr frequency; the measured face of Schroedinger evolution.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Separated oscillatory fields: phase accumulated by a two-level system between two interaction zones, the method behind atomic clocks.

rows.label: MEASURED
rows.note: Spin echoes: free precession of spins refocused by a pulse; unitary two-level evolution measured in time.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Canonical quantum gravity: the Hamiltonian constraint H Psi = 0, the equation with no time in it.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Evolution without evolution: conditioning a stationary global state on a clock subsystem recovers Schroedinger evolution.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: Photonic illustration of Page-Wootters time from entanglement; the only realisation to date.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Quantum reference frames: covariance of physical laws under changes of quantum frame; which clock is a frame-dependent question.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Preprint arguing a 'preferred-time problem' remains in Page-Wootters constructions; PROPOSED at most until peer review.

rows.label: DERIVED
rows.note: Interferometric visibility of a clock in superposition of heights: V = |cos(Delta E Delta tau / 2 hbar)|; a proposal, derived.

rows.label: SINGLE RESULT
rows.note: A self-interfering clock as a which-path witness: visibility loss from a clock-rate difference made by a magnetic gradient, not gravity.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Superposition of proper times in trapped-atom interferometers: predicted visibility modulation and resonance shift; not realised.

rows.label: PROPOSED
rows.note: Quantum signatures of proper time in optical ion clocks ('proper time interferometry'); a proposal, not a measurement.
